cards.front: How many questions are on CON 3990V?
cards.more: Drawn at random from a large bank.

cards.front: How long is CON 3990V?
cards.more: Includes the tutorial, breaks and review: about 72 seconds per question.

cards.front: Passing score on CON 3990V?
cards.more: Pass or fail. The FY26 average was 74.8%.

cards.front: Is CON 3990V open book?
cards.more: No FAR, notes, phone or computer.

cards.front: How many exam attempts are allowed?
cards.back: 3 in 12 months, at least 30 days apart
cards.more: A fourth may be authorized a year after the first failed attempt.

cards.front: What must you take after failing CON 3990V the first time?
cards.more: CON 3910 is its prerequisite.

cards.front: The five required courses?
cards.more: CON 7300V became required on 1 October 2026.

cards.front: How much experience does certification need?
cards.more: A representative sample of the competencies; your component decides what counts.

cards.front: How long do you have to get certified?
cards.more: From entering a contracting-coded position. Many units set a 6-month goal for courses and the exam.

cards.front: Continuous learning after certification?
cards.more: DPCAP recommends at least 40 on contracting topics.

cards.front: Biggest exam area?
cards.more: Then Award 40, Post-Award 38, Pre-Award 30.

cards.front: Which FAR part does the exam FAQ say to read thoroughly?
Where do Army members apply for WarU courses and the exam?
cards.more: Then supervisor and training office approval.

cards.front: How long do you have to test after Pearson's Authorization to Test?
Who can change a contract's price or delivery date?
cards.back: Only the contracting officer, by written modification

cards.front: A COR tells the contractor to add work. What is it?
cards.back: An unauthorized direction: possibly a constructive change or unauthorized commitment
cards.more: CORs cannot change contracts.

cards.front: Who ratifies an unauthorized commitment?
cards.back: The head of the contracting activity, delegable no lower than the chief of the contracting office

cards.front: Who certifies that funds are available?
cards.more: No award or added-cost modification without certified funds.

cards.front: Who makes the source selection decision?
cards.back: The source selection authority (often the contracting officer)

cards.front: Who approves a $50 million DoW justification?
Who audits contractor proposals and costs for DoW?
Who administers many contracts at contractor plants?
Who sets small business size standards?
Who decides bid protests in 100 days?
Who hears DoW contractors' appeals of final decisions?
cards.back: The ASBCA (90 days) or the Court of Federal Claims (12 months)

cards.front: Who approves your training requests in AITAS?
cards.back: Your supervisor, then your Acquisition Training Office

title: Contract types
sub: Match the description to the type

cards.front: One price, whatever it costs the contractor
cards.more: Most risk on the contractor (FAR 16.202).

cards.front: Fixed price that moves with named market changes like fuel prices
Target cost, target profit, ceiling price and a share ratio
Allowable costs plus a fee set at award
Allowable costs plus a fee based on a subjective performance rating
Allowable costs plus a fee that moves with cost results
Hourly rates that include profit, plus materials at cost
cards.more: Least preferred; needs a determination and ceiling (FAR 16.601).

cards.front: A minimum and a maximum quantity, filled by orders
All of the Government's actual needs for an item from one contractor
Lets work start at once, with terms agreed later
Terms set in advance; each call is a contract
Which types are used for commercial products and services?
cards.back: Firm-fixed-price or fixed-price with economic price adjustment

title: B2B Jeopardy review
sub: The class Jeopardy board, answered and checked against the RFO

cards.front: Which FAR part would you recommend to a requiring activity for market research?
cards.more: 10.001 sets when it is required.

cards.front: Which FAR parts cover conflicts of interest?
cards.back: Part 3 (personal conflicts, procurement integrity) and subpart 9.5 (organizational conflicts of interest)

cards.front: What does FAR Part 5 cover?
cards.more: Presolicitation notices, solicitation posting and award notices on SAM.gov.

cards.front: For authority to modify a contract, which FAR part?
cards.more: Only contracting officers acting within their authority may modify (43.202). Their authority itself is in subpart 1.4.

cards.front: Where in the FAR are terminations?
Using a procedure that is inconsistent with the FAR is called...
cards.more: FAR 1.301; individual 1.303, class 1.304.

cards.front: A contract type with low cost risk to the contractor?
cards.more: Firm-fixed-price puts the most cost risk on the contractor.

cards.front: A unique number identifying each solicitation, contract, agreement or order?
cards.more: FAR 4.201. Amendments and modifications get a supplementary number.

cards.front: Termination when a commercial contractor fails to deliver?
cards.more: Noncommercial contracts are terminated for default.

cards.front: In the RFO FAR, what replaced the term "discussions"?
cards.more: Competitive negotiations with offerors in the competitive range (15.204-2).

cards.front: The two types of negotiated acquisition?
Exchange types in FAR Part 15 under the RFO?
cards.back: Early exchanges with industry before receipt; after receipt, clarifications and negotiations
cards.more: "Communications" is no longer a separate step (15.101, 15.202, 15.204).

cards.front: Contract format used in Part 15 for noncommercial contracts?
Order of a Part 15 source selection with negotiations?
cards.back: Receive, evaluate (clarify as needed), set the competitive range, negotiate, get proposal revisions, evaluate, decide, award, notify, debrief

cards.front: Days to request a preaward debriefing after exclusion from the competitive range?
Solicitation used for FAR Part 14?
Solicitation used for FAR Part 15?
Solicitation used for simplified procedures (Parts 12 and 13)?
cards.back: Request for quotations (RFQ), followed by a purchase order

cards.front: Evaluation factors in a Part 14 sealed bid are always...
Is a quotation an offer?
cards.more: The purchase order is the Government's offer; the contract forms when the supplier accepts (12.201-1(b)).

cards.front: Which UCF sections are only in the solicitation?
cards.back: Part IV: Sections K, L and M
cards.more: Section K is incorporated into the contract by reference.

cards.front: Where are the CLINs in the UCF?
Where are documents, exhibits and other attachments listed?
Where are contract clauses in the UCF?
A contractor looks for the PWS in the solicitation. Which section?
Noncommercial order for supplies or services under simplified procedures (DoW)?
cards.back: DD 1155 (the FAR form is the OF 347)

cards.front: Solicitation, offer and award for construction?
Weighted guidelines?
Facilities capital cost of money?
Contract security classification specification?
